name: ui-forge
content:
---
name: ui-forge
description: >-
  Build MAGNIFICENT, award-caliber (Awwwards-level) UIs for any product — landing pages, SaaS dashboards, e-commerce, portfolios, mobile app UIs, and complete multi-page templates (landing→dashboard→404). v2 adds Three.js Scroll Worlds (scroll-driven camera journeys through one 3D scene) and ambient particles (leaves, pointer trails, orbs). 3D scroll effects (parallax, tilt, scroll-jack) are ON by default, plus animated navigation, magnetic/tilt/ripple micro-interactions, Lenis+GSAP smooth scrolling, REAL media via the Higgsfield MCP (procedural fallbacks) and live deployment via website MCPs. Triggers on any request to design, build, or redesign a UI: 'landing page', 'make it premium/cinematic', 'scroll animations', 'scroll world', 'fly-through', '3D journey', 'particle effects', 'animated navbar', 'mobile app UI', 'full template', 'generate a hero image', 'ship it live'.
---

# UI Forge — Award-Caliber UI Engineering

Follow the phased workflow below in order. Load reference files only when you reach their phase (progressive disclosure). Distilled from 171 award-level designs; every token has proven hex values — never invent palette colors.

## Defaults that apply unless the user says otherwise

- **3D scroll layer is ON by default.** Every landing/hero/primary page gets smooth scroll (Lenis), scroll-driven parallax depth, and at least one 3D effect (perspective tilt, z-depth parallax, horizontal scroll-jack on desktop, or camera dolly). Only skip it when the user explicitly declines animations/3D, the page is a utility screen (settings, auth, table), or `prefers-reduced-motion` applies.
- **Scroll World escalation.** When the request smells like a spatial narrative — "scroll world", "fly-through", "3D journey", "travel through", or the product's story genuinely suits moving a camera through space (exploration, systems, archives, planets, cities, products-in-space) — escalate the primary page to the Three.js Scroll World tier (Phase 4-W). It is a page architecture, not a garnish: the whole page scrolls through one continuous WebGL scene. Never bolt it onto an ordinary landing page and never use it for utility pages.
- **Particle ambience for dark heroes.** Dark cinematic heroes (AI, crypto, futuristic, seasonal) get exactly one ambient particle layer from `assets/particle-effects.js` — falling leaves, pointer trail, or floating orbs — chosen to serve the theme. Light/corporate themes skip particles. All particle layers are decorative-only, ≤60 particles, and vanish under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Real media, never placeholders.** Gray boxes and hotlinked stock are defects. When the Higgsfield MCP connector is available, generate on-palette imagery/video/3D per `references/asset-generation.md` (it costs the user credits — follow that file's consent rules); otherwise build the procedural fallbacks in its §7. Either way every media slot ships filled.
- **Complete pages by default.** When the user asks for an app, site, template, or "the whole UI", deliver the full page set from `references/page-templates.md` — never a single page with dead links. Every nav item, footer link, and CTA must resolve to a real page or state.
- **Mobile parity.** Every web build is verified at 375px; when the request is a mobile app UI, use `references/mobile-ui-patterns.md` as the primary source of structure.

## Tech-stack routing (decide first)

- **Default:** React + Tailwind CSS + Framer Motion (component animation) + GSAP ScrollTrigger (scroll-driven) + Lenis (smooth scroll).
- **Fallback:** vanilla HTML/CSS/JS — use `assets/motion-utils.js` (framework-agnostic) + `assets/tokens.css`.
- **Scroll World tier:** React + Tailwind + Three.js + @react-three/fiber + @react-three/drei + GSAP ScrollTrigger + Lenis. Use ONLY when the Scroll World escalation above fires — the narrative must earn the WebGL cost. Vanilla Three.js variant exists for no-build demos (see `references/threejs-scroll-world.md`). Budget: Three.js + scene code ≤ 1MB on disk (~300KB gzipped).
- **CSS-3D (`perspective` + `translateZ`):** for ordinary pages wanting depth, fake it with CSS — cheaper and more reliable than WebGL. Reserve true WebGL for the Scroll World tier or an explicitly requested R3F scene.
- **Mobile web/app UI:** same stack, constrained to a 390–430px shell with safe-area insets; structures from `references/mobile-ui-patterns.md`.

## Phase 1 — Brief extraction

Extract from the request (or infer from the product): **domain** (fintech, AI, food, health, luxury…), **mood** (trust, energy, calm, opulence), **audience** (developers, consumers, enterprise), **form factor** (web landing, dashboard, mobile app, or full multi-page template), and **scope** (single page vs. complete page set — when in doubt and the user said "app/site/template", treat as complete set). Run the **Scroll World check**: set `scrollWorld: true` only when the user asked for one or the narrative genuinely benefits from a camera moving through space; a flag set here changes Phase 4 routing. If the domain is ambiguous, pick the closest row in the domain table in `references/theme-derivation.md` — do not stall asking questions.

## Phase 2 — Theme derivation

Load **`references/theme-derivation.md`**. Classify the domain → pick a proven palette bundle (14 bundles with hex) or derive tokens with the 8-step method → choose the type voice + Google Fonts pairing → copy spacing/radius/shadow/motion tokens. Start from **`assets/tokens.css`** and set `[data-theme]` values. Rules that separate award-level from average: ONE accent color; one type family with 400/800 weight contrast; negative letter-spacing on display type; 4px spacing scale; one dominant element per screen; light themes separate with shadows, dark themes with 1px borders + glow. When `scrollWorld: true`, the 3D world palette and the DOM UI palette must live in the same hue family — derive both from the same bundle.

## Phase 3 — Layout composition (web, mobile, or full template)

- **Web pages:** load **`references/layout-blueprints.md`**. Pick ONE hero archetype (split, centered stack, full-bleed, blob/organic) and follow the universal landing section sequence (navbar → hero → logo cloud → features → showcase → stats → testimonials → pricing → CTA → footer), or the dashboard shell. Copy the ASCII wireframe + Tailwind skeleton, then substitute your theme tokens.
- **Scroll World pages:** the layout IS the beat ledger — skip hero archetypes and instead architect 5–7 story beats per `references/threejs-scroll-world.md` §Story architecture. Conversion sections (pricing, CTA, footer) live in normal DOM after the world ends.
- **Mobile app UI:** load **`references/mobile-ui-patterns.md`**. Pick a platform doctrine (iOS / Material / hybrid), ONE navigation model (tab bar default), then compose screens from the domain blueprint catalog (§4: onboarding, finance, social, food, smart home, chat, AI console, player, reader, game, profile…).
- **Complete template / whole app or site:** load **`references/page-templates.md`**. Select the product row in the page-set matrix and build ALL its pages with shared chrome, plus loading/empty/error states, using the secondary-page skeletons (pricing, auth, onboarding, settings, table, detail, blog, contact, 404, checkout).

## Phase 3.5 — Media & asset layer

Load **`references/asset-generation.md`**. Derive the project's media-DNA prompt line from the active theme, write the shot list (hero key visual, ambient loop, cutouts, avatars, textures, optional GLB — ≤8 assets), get the user's go-ahead when spending credits, then run the batch pipeline (`generate_image_batch`/`generate_video_batch` → `jobs_wait` → one `show_generation_by_ids`) and embed the returned URLs with the zero-CLS patterns in that file. No connector → its §7 fallback ladder. Assets must exist before Phase 4 so motion can choreograph them.

## Phase 4 — Motion & 3D layer (default-on)

Load **`references/motion-3d-playbook.md`** (copy-paste recipes). Minimum bar for "premium": smooth scroll (Lenis synced to ScrollTrigger), hero entrance choreography (staggered reveal + clip-path masks), scroll reveals at 15% viewport, and hover micro-interactions on every interactive element. **Unless the user opted out, add at least one 3D scroll effect** on the primary page: perspective tilt, z-depth parallax, horizontal scroll-jack (desktop only), or camera dolly. On mobile/touch: no scroll-jacking — native vertical scroll with parallax layers clamped to ≤60px depth. Then pick **exactly ONE signature scene** for the primary page from **`references/signature-scenes.md`** (scroll-scrubbed video, card deck, color-morph journey, shader hero, GLB orbit stage…) using its picker table — one show-stopper, executed flawlessly; never two. Dark heroes additionally get one particle layer per playbook §10. Reference implementation: **`assets/Hero3D.jsx`**; vanilla helpers: **`assets/motion-utils.js`**.

## Phase 4-W — Three.js Scroll World (only when `scrollWorld: true`)

Replaces the signature scene — the world IS the show-stopper; adding a second one violates the one-per-page rule. Load **`references/threejs-scroll-world.md`** (full architecture) and **`assets/ScrollWorld3D.jsx`** (annotated React reference). Non-negotiable contract, enforced there in detail:

1. One scene, one perspective camera, one renderer, one world group. Scroll progress drives camera position/target, object rotation, lights, and scene state via GSAP ScrollTrigger scrub or drei `useScroll`.
2. 5–7 story beats, each mapped to a normalized scroll range; the hero object carries the product metaphor (sculpture, machine, archive, constellation, city, product, planetary system).
3. Native reversible scrolling — never hijack the wheel; scroll only drives time.
4. Lazy-mount the canvas; pause RAF off-screen; dispose geometry/materials/textures/renderer on teardown; cap DPR at 2 (1.5 mobile).
5. Static CSS/SVG poster fallback whenever WebGL fails or `prefers-reduced-motion` applies.
6. Run the three art-direction studies before committing — the generic glowing-blue-planet-in-space default is rejected unless the brief specifically earns it.

## Phase 5 — Completeness pass (multi-page deliveries)

1. Walk every link/button on every page — each resolves to a real page, sheet, or state; zero dead `#` links.
2. Shared chrome (navbar/footer/tab bar) pixel-identical across pages; tokens consistent.
3. Data pages ship loading skeleton + empty state + error state; forms ship validation + success feedback.
4. Utility pages (auth, settings) get entrance transitions only — save the heavy 3D for primary surfaces.
5. Follow the handoff checklist in `references/page-templates.md` §5.

## Phase 6 — Quality gate (check every item before delivering)

1. **Contrast:** body text ≥ 4.5:1; muted text used only for non-critical labels; white text on accent passes.
2. **Hierarchy:** exactly one dominant element per viewport; H1 uses `--fs-display` with `letter-spacing: -0.03em`.
3. **Spacing rhythm:** all spacing from the 4px scale; sections pad 96–128px desktop / 64px mobile; max content width 1120–1280px.
4. **Token discipline:** all colors/radii/shadows come from tokens — zero hard-coded hex in components.
5. **Performance:** animations touch ONLY `transform` + `opacity`; never width/height/top/left in scroll handlers; `will-change` used sparingly; 3D/canvas layers lazy-mounted (IntersectionObserver) and paused off-screen.
6. **Reduced motion:** every animation recipe includes a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback — smooth scroll, parallax, marquee, particles, and ambient effects must be disabled under it.
7. **Interaction coverage:** every button/link/card has hover + active + focus-visible states derived from tokens.
8. **Media:** every image has `alt` + explicit dimensions or `aspect-ratio` (zero CLS); non-hero media lazy-loads; hero asset gets `fetchpriority="high"`; video is muted + `playsinline` + real poster, paused off-screen and under reduced motion; total generated payload ≤ 2.5MB above the fold; zero gray placeholders or dead media slots.
9. **Responsive & mobile:** verify at 375px and 1440px; horizontal scroll-jacked sections degrade to vertical stacks on mobile; mobile builds also pass the mobile quality gate in `references/mobile-ui-patterns.md` §5 (safe areas, 44px targets, sheet dismissals, peek affordances).
10. **WebGL discipline (Scroll World / any Three.js layer):** DPR capped at 2 (1.5 mobile); canvas lazy-mounted and RAF cancelled when not intersecting; `geometry/material/texture/renderer.dispose()` on teardown; resize handler updates aspect + size (never stretches); static poster renders when WebGL is unavailable or reduced motion applies; total Three.js + scene payload ≤ 1MB.
11. **Scroll-world integrity (when `scrollWorld: true`):** wheel/touch scrolling stays native and reversible; every beat's DOM copy stays readable over the canvas (text-shadow or glass panel); one dominant object per beat; no continuous ambient spin unless it serves the metaphor — scroll is the sole conductor.

## Worked example (compressed)

**Brief:** "Build a cinematic scroll-world site for Nimbus, an AI code-review tool — fly through the codebase."
**Flow:** Phase 1: domain AI/dev, mood technical power, single landing, `scrollWorld: true` ("fly through"). Phase 2: `neon-trading` bundle, Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono, world + DOM share the violet family. Phase 3: beat ledger — hook (enter the archive) → origin → system → conflict → proof → CTA; pricing/footer in DOM after the world. Phase 3.5: batch-generate poster key visual + 4 avatars. Phase 4-W: camera arcs around an icosahedral "codebase core" per `ScrollWorld3D.jsx`, beats scrubbed by `useScroll`, floating-orbs particle layer, static poster fallback. Phase 6: gates 10–11 pass (DPR 2, dispose on unmount, native scroll, readable glass panels). Closing note offers the calmer CSS-3D variant if WebGL feels heavy.

## Phase 7 — Ship (only when the user wants it live)

Static builds deploy through connected MCPs: Higgsfield websites (`create_website` → follow its creation instructions → commit/push → `deploy_website`), or Vercel/Replit connectors. Before publishing anywhere, fill real OG metadata and generate the `og_image` via Phase 3.5. Never deploy without the user asking.

## Files

| File | Load when |
|---|---|
| `references/theme-derivation.md` | Phase 2 — palettes, type, token scales, domain mapping |
| `references/layout-blueprints.md` | Phase 3 — web wireframes + HTML/Tailwind skeletons |
| `references/mobile-ui-patterns.md` | Phase 3 — mobile doctrines, nav models, gestures, 13 domain screen blueprints, mobile quality gate |
| `references/page-templates.md` | Phase 3 + 5 — complete page-set matrix + skeletons for every secondary page (multi-page/template deliveries) |
| `references/asset-generation.md` | Phase 3.5 — Higgsfield media pipeline, prompts-from-tokens, embed patterns, fallback ladder |
| `references/motion-3d-playbook.md` | Phase 4 — all animation/3D recipes incl. §9 scroll-world quickstart + §10 particles |
| `references/signature-scenes.md` | Phase 4 — the one-per-page show-stopper library (12 scenes + Scroll World escalation) |
| `references/threejs-scroll-world.md` | Phase 4-W — full scroll-world architecture, beat ledger, R3F + vanilla patterns, art direction, mobile degradation |
| `assets/tokens.css` | Phase 2 — starter token stylesheet, themes via `[data-theme]` |
| `assets/motion-utils.js` | Phase 4 — vanilla JS helpers (magnetic, tilt, reveals, Lenis+GSAP init, cursor glow) |
| `assets/Hero3D.jsx` | Phase 4 — annotated React reference hero with layered 3D parallax |
| `assets/ScrollWorld3D.jsx` | Phase 4-W — annotated React scroll-world reference (beats, camera path, poster fallback) |
| `assets/particle-effects.js` | Phase 4 — falling leaves, pointer trail, floating orbs (reduced-motion-safe, cleanup-returning) |

Repo meta (`README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, `install.sh`) documents installation and versioning — never loaded at runtime.

# Asset Generation — Real Images, Video & 3D in Every Build Award-level UIs are media-rich: real key visuals, ambient video, floating product cutouts, believable avatars. This file turns the theme tokens into an art-directed media pipeline. Primary engine: the **Higgsfield MCP connector** (image / video / 3D / audio generation). When it isn't connected, use §7's procedural fallback ladder — **never ship gray placeholder boxes or hotlinked stock**. ## 0. Rules before spending anything 1. **Credits are the user's money.** Generation runs on the user's Higgsfield credits. Generate when the user asked for imagery/video/cinematic quality or approved your proposed shot list; otherwise propose the shot list first ("I can generate a hero visual + ambient loop + 3 avatars — want me to?"). For >3 assets or any video, preflight with `get_cost: true` and surface the number. 2. **Never pass `use_unlim: true` on your own initiative** — omit it and let the server ask. 3. Higgsfield tools are a third-party connector: if they aren't available in the session, don't stall — fall back (§7) and note the upgrade path to the user. 4. Every generated asset must obey the **media quality gate** (SKILL.md Phase 6, item 9): explicit `width/height` or `aspect-ratio` (zero CLS), lazy-load all non-hero media, `alt` text, video muted + `playsinline` + poster + paused off-screen and under `prefers-reduced-motion`. ## 1. Art-direction contract (tokens → prompts) Every prompt inherits the theme so media looks *designed in*, not pasted on. Build one **media DNA** line per project and append it to every prompt: `". ``` Non-hero media: add `loading="lazy"` and drop `fetchpriority`. ### 4b. Ambient video hero (polite by default) ```html ``` Reduced motion shows the poster — which is why the poster must be a real generated still, not a black frame. Scroll-scrubbed video: `signature-scenes.md` S1. ### 4c. Floating cutout stack (depth without WebGL) ```html
``` Then attach playbook §6a tilt or §2c z-parallax to `.stack-obj`. ### 4d. Generated GLB in a build Vanilla (ES modules CDN): ```html ``` React: `useGLTF("MODEL_URL.glb")` via `@react-three/drei` inside R3F (only when the user asked for true WebGL — SKILL.md routing). Full orbit stage recipe: `signature-scenes.md` S11. Keep meshes < 5MB; lazy-mount the canvas (IntersectionObserver) and pause the RAF loop off-screen. ### 4e. UI sound layer (optional, off by default) Only when the user asks for sound: `generate_audio` (`seed_audio`) can voice a short product line for a demo scene. Never autoplay audio; gate strictly behind a click on a visible mute-toggle. Skip SFX entirely — this connector is speech-only. ## 5. Runtime-generated imagery inside AI artifacts (advanced) For claude.ai artifacts that should create imagery **at runtime** (e.g. "generate my banner" button), call the Anthropic API from the artifact with the Higgsfield MCP attached and have Claude run the generation: ```js const r = await fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ model: "claude-sonnet-4-6", max_tokens: 1000, messages: [{ role: "user", content: promptForImage }], mcp_servers: [{ type: "url", url: "https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp", name: "higgsfield" }], }), }); const data = await r.json(); const urls = data.content.filter(b => b.type === "mcp_tool_result") .flatMap(b => (b.content?.[0]?.text?.match(/https:\/\/\S+\.(png|jpe?g|webp|mp4)/g) ?? [])); ``` Label the control clearly ("uses your Higgsfield credits") and handle the no-connector error path. ## 6. Ship it live (when the user wants a URL) Static builds can be deployed straight through connected MCPs: **Higgsfield websites** (`create_website` → follow `get_website_creation_instructions` → commit/push → `deploy_website`; `publish_website` only lists the already-live build on the feed) or **Vercel / Replit** connectors when present. Fill real OG metadata before publishing — generate the `og_image_url` with this pipeline. ## 7. Fallback ladder (no Higgsfield connected) 1. **SVG mesh-gradient + film grain** — hero-grade backdrop from pure tokens: ```html ``` 2. **Pure-CSS aurora** (playbook §8a) + grain (§8b) when even SVG feels heavy. 3. **Canvas generative art** — particles (§8d) or the shader-gradient signature scene (S7) as the "key visual". 4. **Hand-drawn SVG product glyphs** — outline illustrations in `--accent` with S6 line-draw as the reveal. 5. **CSS device mock + typographic screenshot** — fake the app UI in HTML inside a device frame instead of a screenshot image. The ladder is also the **reduced-data path**: prefer it for backgrounds even when generation is available, and spend generated media on foreground subjects the user will actually look at.
references.references/mobile-ui-patterns.md:
# Mobile UI Patterns — Study & Build Guide Complete mobile UI vocabulary: every navigation model, component pattern, gesture, and per-domain screen blueprint. Use alongside `theme-derivation.md` (tokens) and `motion-3d-playbook.md` (motion). All skeletons are HTML/Tailwind mobile-web (375–430px viewport) — the same structures map 1:1 to React Native / Flutter widgets. --- ## 0. Platform doctrine (never mix blindly) | Concern | iOS (HIG) | Android (Material 3) | |---|---|---| | Nav bar | Bottom tab bar, 49pt, blur material | Navigation bar, 80dp, tonal surface | | Back affordance | Top-left chevron + swipe-from-left-edge | System back button/gesture | | Corners | Continuous (squircle), 10–39px radii | Shape scale 4–28dp | | Primary buttons | Rounded rect or capsule, tinted | Filled / tonal pill, state layers | | Sheets | Detents (medium/large), grabber | Modal bottom sheet, drag handle | | Typography | SF Pro — 17pt body, semibold nav titles | Roboto/M3 type scale | | Haptics | Impact/notification feedback per action | Vibration effects, subtler | Pick ONE doctrine per product unless the user asks for a hybrid. Mobile-web hybrid default: iOS-style tab bar + capsule CTAs + M3-style state layers on press. **Safe areas:** always pad with `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. Tab bar: `padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`. Status bar overlays: `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)`. **Touch targets:** ≥44×44px. Primary CTA height 48–56px. One-thumb reach: put primary actions in the bottom 60% of the screen. --- ## 1. Navigation models (pick ONE primary) ### 1.1 Bottom tab bar — the default 3–5 tabs. Active tab: accent icon + label; inactive: muted. Center tab can be a raised FAB (camera/compose). ```html
Home
``` ### 1.2 Top segmented control For 2–4 sibling views (Feed/Discover, Daily/Weekly). Pill track, sliding indicator (layoutId in Framer Motion; CSS `transform` transition in vanilla). ### 1.3 Stack navigation + large title iOS pattern: nav title starts 34pt bold inline with content, collapses to centered 17pt semibold on scroll. Implement with a scroll listener toggling two headers. ### 1.4 Drawer / side rail Only for 6+ sections or enterprise tools. On mobile-web: slide-over panel with scrim, `translateX` animation, focus-trapped. ### 1.5 Gesture-first (no visible chrome) Stories/swipe decks (card decks, short-video feeds). Always include a first-run hint (coach mark) and an escape button. --- ## 2. Core component patterns ### Sheets & modals - **Bottom sheet** (default modal on mobile): slides up, scrim 40% black, drag-to-dismiss, detents 40%/90%, 28px top radius. - **Action sheet**: list of destructive/neutral actions + separated Cancel. - **Full-screen modal**: only for focused creation (compose, checkout) — X top-left, primary action top-right or sticky bottom. ```html
``` ### Lists & cards - **Inset grouped list** (settings): rounded-16 sections on `bg-bg`, rows 44–56px, chevron right, separators inset 16px. - **Feed card**: image 4:3 or 16:9 rounded-20, title 17px semibold, meta row muted 13px, icon action row. - **Horizontal rail**: snap-scroll (`snap-x snap-mandatory`), card width 75–85% so the next card peeks. Peek = affordance. ### Inputs & forms - One field per row, 16px text (prevents iOS zoom), input height 48–52px. - Sticky bottom primary CTA above keyboard. - OTP: 4–6 segmented boxes, auto-advance, paste fill. - Toggles: iOS-style switch (accent when on), 51×31px pill. ### Feedback - **Toast/snackbar**: bottom, above tab bar, auto-dismiss 3s, one action max. - **Skeletons over spinners**: shimmer blocks matching the final layout for any load >300ms. - **Empty states**: icon/illustration 80px, one-line headline, one-line sub, one CTA. Never a bare "No data". - **Pull-to-refresh**: spinner synced to drag distance. --- ## 3. Gesture & motion vocabulary (mobile) | Gesture | Use | Motion | |---|---|---| | Tap | all actions | scale 0.97, 120ms | | Long-press | context menu / preview | haptic + scale-in menu from touch point | | Swipe horizontal | card deck, tab change, list actions | follow finger, spring release | | Swipe down | dismiss sheet/photo, refresh | translateY follows finger, scrim fades | | Pinch | photo/map zoom | transform scale, clamp 0.5–3× | | Edge swipe (left) | back | interactive pop transition | Mobile hero motion: entrance stagger (eyebrow → headline → sub → CTA → visual, 80ms steps), hero visual floats on a 4px y-loop, scroll parallax on decorative blobs only. 3D scroll effects from `motion-3d-playbook.md` apply on mobile too, but clamp `translateZ` depths ≤60px and never scroll-jack on touch — use native vertical scroll with parallax layers instead. --- ## 4. Domain screen blueprints (the full idea catalog) Each entry: structure + the ONE thing that makes it award-level. ### 4.1 Onboarding / auth Splash → 3–5 swipeable value slides (illustration + headline + page dots) → sign-up (social first, email last) → OTP → permission priming (explain WHY before the system prompt). Award-level: illustration morphs between slides; progress dot expands into a pill. ### 4.2 Social / feed Stories rail (rings for unseen) → infinite feed cards → FAB compose → detail with shared-element transition from the card. Award-level: shared-element hero image + like-button particle burst. ### 4.3 Finance / wallet Balance hero (huge mono number, sparkline) → quick actions row (send/request/scan/top-up as circular icon buttons) → transactions grouped by day with category chips → card screen with a 3D-tilting card. Award-level: balance counts up on load; amounts blur until tapped (privacy toggle). ### 4.4 Health / fitness / yoga Daily ring/progress hero → today's plan as timeline cards → session player (full-bleed video, big timer, minimal chrome) → weekly bar stats. Award-level: breathing-animation circle; rings draw on via stroke-dashoffset. ### 4.5 Food / delivery Sticky search + location header → category chip rail → hero dish carousel (snap) → restaurant cards (image, rating pill, ETA) → dish detail with parallax header that shrinks into the navbar → cart sheet with steppers → live order tracking. Award-level: add-to-cart flies the item into the cart icon. ### 4.6 E-commerce / product 2-col product grid (image 1:1, bold price, wishlist heart) → product page: gallery pager → title/price → color/size chips → sticky bottom "Add to bag" → cart → single-column checkout. Award-level: pointer-tilt product hero; size-chip selection springs. ### 4.7 Smart home / IoT dashboard Room selector chips → device grid cards (icon + name + state + inline toggle) → device detail: BIG radial/slider control center-stage → scenes row. Award-level: draggable radial thermostat dial with haptic ticks; active device cards glow in accent (neumorphic or glass — pick per theme). ### 4.8 Chat / messaging Conversation list (avatar, name, last message, time, unread badge) → thread: grouped bubbles, day separators, sticky input bar → media viewer with pinch-zoom + swipe-down dismiss. Award-level: message send morphs from the input; typing indicator with bouncing dots. ### 4.9 Music / media player Library lists → now-playing: blurred album-art background, big art rounded-24, scrubber, controls (72px play), lyrics sheet. Award-level: background hue extracted from the art; mini-player expands with shared-element. ### 4.10 Reading / novel / docs Cover grid → reader: serif 19px, line-height 1.7, tap zones (prev/next/menu), chapter sheet, theme presets (paper/sepia/dark), hairline progress bar. Award-level: ambient theme that shifts with time of day. ### 4.11 Game UI Hex/tile grids, HUD overlays (health, resources in top corners), bottom ability bar with radial cooldown sweeps. Award-level: floating damage numbers with physics; cooldown sweep via conic-gradient mask. ### 4.12 AI chat / agent console Thread list → chat: user right-bubbles, agent left with avatar, streaming text reveal, tool-call cards (collapsible, status → result), code blocks with copy, sticky composer with model-picker chip. Award-level: "thinking" shimmer state; tool cards expand inline with spring; text streams in word-by-word. ### 4.13 Profile / settings Header (avatar 88px, name, handle, edit) → stats row → content tabs or inset grouped list. Settings: destructive actions separated in red, version line in footer. Award-level: stretchy header — avatar parallax-zooms on pull-down. --- ## 5. Mobile quality gate (in addition to SKILL.md Phase 5) 1. Safe-area insets on ALL fixed chrome (tab bar, sheets, sticky CTAs). 2. Every interactive element ≥44px; primary CTA reachable one-handed. 3. Text inputs ≥16px font (no iOS auto-zoom). 4. Sheets dismiss by drag AND scrim tap AND back button. 5. Skeletons for all async content; optimistic UI for likes/sends/toggles. 6. Horizontal rails always show a peek of the next item. 7. No scroll-jacking on touch; parallax depth ≤60px; everything honors `prefers-reduced-motion`. 8. Test at 375×667 (SE) and 430×932 (Pro Max). Content must never hide behind the tab bar — bottom padding = tab bar height + safe area.

# Page Templates — Complete Multi-Page Delivery Contract

When the user asks for "the full UI", "complete pages", "a whole template", or builds an app/product site, deliver a COMPLETE page set — never a single hero page with placeholder links. This file defines what "complete" means per product type and gives skeletons for every secondary page.

---

## 1. Completeness rules

1. **Every nav item and CTA on a page must resolve to a real page/state.** Dead links and `#` hrefs are a defect. In static previews, use hash routing or in-app navigation so every route works.
2. **Minimum viable complete set:** primary page + every page reachable in one click from it + auth (if the product has accounts) + 404/empty states.
3. **Shared chrome is identical across pages:** same navbar, footer, tokens, motion system. Extract it once, reuse everywhere.
4. **Each page still gets ONE dominant element** and the full Phase 2 theme — secondary pages are not excuses for plain design.
5. **States, not just screens:** every list/table ships with loading skeleton, empty state, and error state; every form ships with validation + success feedback.

## 2. Page-set matrix (pick the product row, build ALL its pages)

| Product | Required pages |
|---|---|
| Marketing / landing site | Home · Features/Product · Pricing · About/Story · Blog index + post · Contact · Legal (privacy/terms) · 404 |
| SaaS app | Landing · Login · Signup · Forgot password · Onboarding wizard · Dashboard home · Core feature pages (2–4) · Settings (profile/billing/notifications) · Empty + error states |
| Mobile app UI | Onboarding (3–5 slides) · Login/OTP · Home tab · 2–4 remaining tabs · Key detail screen · Sheet/modal flows · Profile/settings — per `mobile-ui-patterns.md` |
| E-commerce | Home · Category/grid · Product detail · Cart · Checkout (address → payment → confirm) · Order success · Account/orders · 404 |
| Dashboard / admin / AI console | Login · Overview (KPIs + charts) · Data table page (filter/sort/paginate) · Detail/entity page · Live activity or console feed · Settings · Empty/error states |
| Portfolio | Home · Work index · Case-study detail · About · Contact · 404 |
| Docs / knowledge base | Docs home (search hero) · Article page (sidebar TOC, prev/next) · Changelog · 404 |

## 3. Secondary page skeletons

### 3.1 Pricing
Eyebrow + headline → billing toggle (monthly/yearly, yearly shows "save 20%") → 3 tier cards (middle elevated: accent border, scale-105, "Most popular" pill) → feature checklist rows with ✓ → FAQ accordion → final CTA band. Award-level: toggle animates prices counting; recommended card has slow ambient glow.

### 3.2 Auth (login / signup / forgot)
Split layout: left = form card (logo, headline "Welcome back", social buttons → divider → email/password → submit → footer link swap login/signup), right = brand panel with product visual or animated gradient. Mobile: form only, brand panel becomes a compact header. Award-level: inputs float labels; submit button morphs to spinner → success check → redirect.

### 3.3 Onboarding wizard (app setup)
3–5 steps, top progress bar or dots, one question per screen, big selectable cards/chips, Back ghost + Continue primary (disabled until valid), final "All set" celebration (confetti or scale-in check). Skippable.

### 3.4 Settings
Sidebar section list (desktop) / inset grouped list (mobile) → panels: Profile (avatar upload, fields), Account (email, password, delete — danger zone separated, red), Notifications (toggle rows), Billing (plan card + invoices table), API/Integrations (key rows with copy + reveal). Award-level: unsaved-changes bar slides up ("Save / Discard").

### 3.5 Data table page
Header (title + primary action "New X") → toolbar (search, filter chips, sort, column toggle) → table (sticky header, row hover, status pill cells, row actions ⋮) → pagination or infinite scroll. States: skeleton rows, empty ("No X yet" + CTA), error banner with retry.

### 3.6 Detail / entity page
Breadcrumb → title row (name + status pill + actions) → stat cards row → tabbed body (Overview / Activity / Settings) → right rail (meta, assignees, timestamps) on desktop, stacked on mobile.

### 3.7 Blog index + post
Index: featured post card (large) + grid of cards (image 16:9, tag chip, title, date · read time). Post: centered 680–720px column, H1 + meta row, hero image, prose styles (h2 anchors, code blocks, pull quotes), author card, prev/next. Award-level: reading-progress hairline bar; headings reveal on scroll.

### 3.8 Contact / about
Contact: split — left headline + channels (email, socials, office), right form card (name/email/message) with inline validation + success state replacing the form. About: story timeline, values grid, team cards with hover photo treatment, stats band.

### 3.9 404 / empty / error
404: oversized display numeral (dominant element), one-line wit, "Back home" primary + search or popular links. Empty: icon 80px + headline + sub + CTA. Error: banner or full-page with retry button and reference ID.

### 3.10 Checkout (3 steps, single column)
Step indicator (1 Address → 2 Payment → 3 Review) → forms with validation → order summary card sticky right (desktop) / collapsible top (mobile) → success page: big animated check, order number, "Track order" + "Continue shopping".

## 4. Navigation between pages

- **React (webapp-building):** routes wired in App.tsx with the provided router — every page is a real component in `src/pages/`.
- **Vanilla HTML:** one folder, `index.html` links to sibling pages (`pricing.html`, …); identical header/footer markup on each; motion via `assets/motion-utils.js` auto-init.
- **Mobile shell:** bottom tab bar on every tab page; detail pages push over with back chevron (see `mobile-ui-patterns.md` §1.3).

## 5. Handoff checklist for "complete template" deliveries

1. Every route in the nav/footer/CTAs renders real content.
2. Shared chrome consistent; tokens identical on all pages.
3. Loading / empty / error states present on data pages.
4. 3D scroll layer on the primary page (unless opted out), lighter motion on utility pages (auth/settings get entrance transitions only).
5. All pages pass the Phase 5 quality gate + responsive check at 375px and 1440px.
